newsitem.title: UK: Brewer Scottish & Newcastle profits rise.
newsitem.headline: Brewer Scottish & Newcastle profits rise.

text.p: Britain's largest brewer Scottish and Newcastle Plc Monday announced a 26 percent rise in half-year profits to 195.1 million British pounds ($328 million) and said the second half of the year had started positively.
The company's purchase of Courage from Australian brewer Fosters last year helped boost profits from its beer divisions 67 percent push to 89.9 million pounds ($151 million).
The dividend rise to 7.21 pence (12.1 cents) per share beat most analysts' forecasts for a 7 pence (11.8 cents) payout.

"Overall, I think our 10 percent dividend increase, at the top end of the (forecast) range, is a measure of our confidence for the second half of the year," Chief Executive Brian Stewart said in an interview.
"General trading conditions are at least as good as they were this time last year and there has been a bit of an improvement in mainland Europe," he added.
The company's stock rose 7 pence (11.8 cents) to 647 pence ($10.87).
Beer sales fell by just over 1 percent compared with the first half of 1995 which was bolstered by outstanding summer weather, said the company.
Despite this, Scottish and Newcastle said sales of John Smith's, the country's leading ale, were up 17 percent and sales of Foster's lager grew 6.5 percent to its highest ever volume.

Profits from its Scottish and Newcastle's Centre Parcs activity holiday resorts were down 11 percent at about 44 million pounds ($73.9 million) due to a weak economy in mainland Europe and the cost of improving its facilities in the Netherlands and Belgium.
Profits from the company's pubs grew 8.2 percent to 87 million pounds (146.1 million).
